newsitem.title: UK: Scientists prove chemicals cause fish sex-change.
newsitem.headline: Scientists prove chemicals cause fish sex-change.

text.p: Dutch scientists said on Wednesday they had proved environmental chemicals can cause sex changes, at least in fish.

Exposing carp to a chemical sometimes found in sewage caused their sex organs to atrophy and some developed female sex organs, Sylvia Gimeno and colleagues at the TNO-Nutrition and Food Research Institute in Delft said.

Chemicals that mimic the effects of the female hormone oestrogen are widely blamed for "feminising" animals, including fish and alligators. Some researchers believe they could be to blame for declining male fertility in some European cities.
Gimeno's group exposed young fish to a chemical, 4-tert-pentyphenol (TPP), a common industrial chemical. They also exposed another group to oestrogen and a third to plain water.
Both the oestrogen and chemical groups developed an oviduct, which female fish use to lay eggs, they wrote in a letter to the science journal Nature.
They also showed a reduction in germ cells, the cells that later become sperm.

"We have demonstrated, for the first time, that the period of sex differentiation in fish is sensitive to xeno-oestrogen compounds, as shown by the appearance of female... characteristics," they wrote.
They said their test would be good to use to check the effects of other environmental chemicals.
